name: Entity Graph
blurb: Every company, model, paper, person, dataset, benchmark, and regulation as a node.

nodes.scheme: DOI or arXiv id, linked to the original publisher
arXiv id from the model's own tags

reading.body:
The graph contains 23,033 nodes as of August 2026, and the distribution across categories reveals where coverage is dense and where it remains thin.

Open models dominate by volume at 15,247 entries, which is roughly 66 percent of the total node count. API models add 395 more. Papers cited by tracked models, at 1,803, outnumber editorially tracked research papers by more than thirteen to one, meaning most of the scholarly record here arrives indirectly, through what model builders chose to tag rather than through independent curation. State AI bills account for 2,740 nodes, the second-largest category, reflecting how much legislative activity has accumulated around the technology even as the technical infrastructure it governs continues to scale. MCP servers, at 2,056, represent a newer layer of tooling infrastructure that sits between models and applications.

The categories that are sparse matter as much as the ones that are large. Only 37 hardware entries, 17 datasets, and 1 tool appear in the graph. Hardware is where compute originates and where power demand is determined, so 37 curated rows is a narrow window onto that layer. The dataset count of 17 is similarly limited given how many open models the graph tracks. The graph does not claim to be exhaustive in those areas, and the counts confirm it. What the data does show clearly is that the model layer, measured by sheer node count, has expanded far faster than the infrastructure and data layers that support it.
